headings: A possible identification concerns Andrew Allexander. The banns/marriage index records Joannet Glasgow and Andrew Allexander/ on 8 August 1661 at Glasgow.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 644 / 1/230 / 230; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Mergaret Androsoune. The 3 February 1550/51 barn purchase expressly names David Mathy and Mergaret Androsoune as spouses.<ref>Renwick, Abstracts of Protocols of Town Clerks of Glasgow,vol1,protocol71; printed p. 27 (PDF p. 60); [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto01glas/page/n60/mode/1up record].</ref> Inspected printed protocol abstract; original manuscript uninspected. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns William Anderson. The banns/marriage index records Agnas Glasgow and William Anderson on 5 July 1666 at Longformacus.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 750/10 / 79; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

The same 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Neal Anderson, aged 65, with Abraham Anderson, aged 60, and Robert Anderson, aged 50, each identified as brothers within the household. It is relevant as Fan context because Robert Anderson appears as a witness in the 1908 Elder marriage transcription and the Anderson surname also occurs in the Elder marriage network.<ref>Down the Road, Gortereghy 1911 census browse; [https://downtheroad.dev/de/census?county=Antrim&tab=browse&townland=Gortereghy&year=1911 record].</ref> It does not establish a relationship to Alexander Glasgow or to the Glasgow family.

The same reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Neal Anderson, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, marrying Sarah Elder, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, on 28 September 1893. Sarah's father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Nancy Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; [https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0 record].</ref> This is a new parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and is consistent with the 1908 entry naming Alexander Elder as a son of a Robert Elder, but the shared father's identity and any connection to Robert Elder, husband of Mary Glasgow, remain unproved until the original register is inspected.

A possible identification concerns Mary Anderson. A 2007 RootsChat research post reproduces a 18 June 1908 Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage entry for Alexander Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, whose father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer. Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; [https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0 record].</ref> The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Sarah McCaughern. The 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Sarah McCaughern, aged 82, as head of household with Matilda Mulholland, 52, and Caroline McCaughern, 47, recorded as daughters; Sara Jane McCaughern, 45, and Jas Alex McCaughern, 43, are also listed as children, with Geo Mulholland, 14, as grandson. It confirms a substantial McCaughern household in the same townland as the Elder and Glasgow-associated records, but it does not identify Sarah's husband, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Sarah McCaughern. The original 1901 and 1911 returns establish continuity of Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy family. Sarah was a Derry-born widow aged 72/82; Caroline, Sarah J/Sara Jane, James A/Jas Alex, Matilda and grandson George occur in both returns. Elizabeth, 32, is also a daughter in 1901. Sarah [[Dysart-1893]], married in 1851 to Gortereghy farmer John McCaughern, remains the strongest mother identity, but neither census names her deceased husband or maiden surname.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf record]; 1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf record]; Rasharkin Presbyterian civil marriage register 1851; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1851/09402/5405894.pdf record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Robert Elder. These relationships are consistent with the 1901 household, the 1908 marriage and the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial; the family’s later identities remain uncertain.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Robert Elder. The reproduced Third Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Robert Elder, full-age bachelor labourer of Ballymoney, marrying Jane Adams McCaughey, full-age spinster of Garvaghey, on 13 July 1887. Robert's father is recorded as James Elder, labourer; Jane's father as William McCaughey, labourer.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; [https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0 record].</ref> The witnesses were Archie McCaughey and Lizzie Connaghy. This Robert is distinct from Mary Glasgow’s 1871 husband, Robert Elder, whose father was Nathaniel Elder and whose occupation was farmer. The source is a secondary transcription and the original register remains to be inspected. The identification remains uncertain.

A reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records John Elder, full-age bachelor of Rasharkin, marrying Annie Patterson, aged 20, on 12 May 1886. John's father is recorded as John Elder, farmer; Annie's father as David Patterson, farmer.<ref>Second Portglenone Presbyterian civil marriage 1886; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1886/10833/5951328.pdf record].</ref>

A possible identification concerns John Elder. The 1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory lists John Elder, junior, as a grocer and postmaster among the inhabitants of Rasharkin. In the neighbourhood section it separately lists James Elder and James Elder, junior at Ballydonnelly.<ref>1912 Belfast and Ulster Directory, Rasharkin; [https://lennonwylie.co.uk/PT191214.htm record].</ref> They add useful identity clues for separating the later Elder households, but the directory does not identify either man as Robert Elder's son or brother. The source is a directory, not a parentage record. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Robert Elder. The published headstone transcription for Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church records a memorial erected by Alexander Elder of Gortrickey to his father Robert Elder, his mother Jane, and his sisters and brothers. It also records Alexander Elder's death on 5 January 1943.<ref>Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones; [https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html record].</ref> This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Mary. Daniel Glasco, Norfolk planter, conveyed 100 acres to Richard Linton with the consent of Mary, explicitly his wife. The court endorsement says Daniel personally acknowledged the deed on 3 September 1729, establishing survival to that date.<ref>Princess Anne County, Deeds and Wills Book4 Part1 (1724–1735), manuscript p.207, DGS7645780; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-99PX-F3DX record].</ref> Inspected original deed endorsement. Registration alone is not used as a life boundary. The identification remains uncertain.
